assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum-model prediction of flat bands at magic twist angles, followed by the experimental discovery of correlated-insulator and superconducting states in magic-angle bilayer graphene, opened the field of moire quantum materials. The impact is broad, original and clearly stated, with a very large follow-on literature on tunable correlated and topological phases.
assessment.attribution: A natural three-person split: theory prediction (Bistritzer and MacDonald) plus the decisive 2018 experiments (Jarillo-Herrero, whose group also realised the device control). Co-authors and the Harvard/Columbia-style parallel experimental efforts exist, so the experimental share is not wholly unique, but the supplied credit supports a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Roughly eight years since the experiments, with independent reproduction in many laboratories and a stable interpretation of the flat-band origin; timely and clearly mature as an experimental-plus-theory discovery, though the nature of the superconductivity is still debated.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity in twisted graphene remains unsettled
Priority and weight of other experimental and theoretical contributors to twistronics and moire physics are not resolved by the supplied names

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks using magic-wavelength trapping, with many atoms interrogated simultaneously, have pushed fractional frequency uncertainty to the 10^-18 level. The discovery is an enabling invention for precision measurement, redefinition of the second, geodesy and tests of fundamental physics. Importance and clarity are very high.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated it; Ye's group brought the strontium lattice clock to extreme accuracy and coherence. A clean two-person prize is plausible. Interactions with the earlier frequency-comb and ion-clock prizes (Hall, Haensch; Wineland) must be handled carefully; others working on ytterbium lattice clocks are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of development, multiple independent clock groups and international comparisons confirm the results; recognition is timely and the field is mature.
uncertainties: Contributions of other lattice-clock groups (for example ytterbium clocks) not captured in the credited names
Overlap with the earlier prizes for optical frequency combs and ion trapping must be weighed

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators by Kane and Mele, and the experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe wells by Molenkamp's group, founded the topological-materials field. The impact on condensed-matter concepts and on later materials work is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: This configuration pairs the two theorists of Z2 topological order with the decisive first experimental demonstration (König et al., Molenkamp, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal). BHZ theory and the Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3 3D-material discoveries (Hasan, Cava, Shen, Zhang) are not among the credited names, which leaves a real unresolved credit question.
assessment.maturity: Nearly twenty years of independent confirmation, including 3D topological insulators; interpretation is stable. Recognition is mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit for Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and 3D topological insulator experiments is outside this candidate's names
Competing topological-insulator candidate lists on the longlist may split recognition

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED established strong coupling between a superconducting qubit and a microwave resonator and the architecture on which superconducting quantum processors are built. This is a foundational and highly influential invention with experimental and technological reach.
assessment.attribution: Blais supplied the theory proposal, Wallraff and Schoelkopf the first experimental demonstration and the later development of the platform. A three-person prize is workable. The 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits (Clarke, Devoret, Martinis) overlaps in context and the credit boundary versus transmon inventors (Koch, Schoelkopf) needs scrutiny.
assessment.maturity: Platform repeatedly confirmed in many laboratories since 2004; stable interpretation. Timing is reasonable but the 2025 prize may reduce urgency.
uncertainties: Relation to the 2025 prize and to transmon-qubit credit
Whether the discovery or the later engineering of quantum processors is the intended recognition

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of a Higgs boson by ATLAS and CMS completed the Standard Model and was a landmark of experimental particle physics. Its scientific importance is beyond doubt, and as a former accelerator experimentalist I weigh the detector and collaboration achievement heavily, while recognising the 2013 prize already honoured the theoretical prediction.
assessment.attribution: Credit for a discovery by thousands is intrinsically hard to allocate. The supplied names are founding spokespersons and project leaders (ATLAS, CMS) and do not include the physicists coordinating the 2012 analyses or the LHC accelerator leaders. A prize to individuals would be contentious versus an organisation-like honour that the statutes do not allow.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by two independent experiments and measured further for more than a decade; the discovery is mature and the timing arguably late, but properties of the boson are still being refined.
uncertainties: Fair attribution among thousands of collaborators and the accelerator contribution is unresolved
Whether a prize is appropriate given the 2013 award for the theory
I have no connection to ATLAS or CMS recorded; my judgement relies on general knowledge

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of X-ray, optical and radio afterglows of gamma-ray bursts established their extragalactic, cosmological origin and opened multi-messenger transient astrophysics. The result was a decades-old puzzle resolved by a clean observational breakthrough.
assessment.attribution: BeppoSAX (Costa, Frontera) located the X-ray afterglow in 1997 and rapid optical and radio follow-up (Kulkarni and colleagues; van Paradijs, deceased, and others) established distance and energetics. The credited names support a fair configuration though others, including Paczynski (deceased) and Piro, Djorgovski, Frail, contributed.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by thousands of subsequent bursts and the later connection to supernovae and neutron-star mergers; very mature, and timely only if no further delay.
uncertainties: Contributions of deceased and additional observers cannot be recognised and may complicate fairness
Balance between instrument team and ground-based follow-up credit

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Detection of baryon acoustic oscillations in galaxy clustering gave a standard ruler for cosmology and strongly constrained dark energy. The measurement is a clean, widely used probe independent of supernovae and the CMB.
assessment.attribution: The 2005 detections came from SDSS (Eisenstein) and 2dFGRS (Cole, Percival), so this is a two-survey configuration of three authors. Large collaborations, early theoretical groundwork (Peebles, Yu, Sunyaev, Zeldovich) and later BOSS and DESI work leave credit allocation delicate.
assessment.maturity: Repeatedly confirmed by independent surveys; recent DESI hints about evolving dark energy show the application is live, though the BAO detection itself is solid.
uncertainties: Role of theory predecessors and large survey teams
Interpretive questions about dark energy are still being tested

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's discovery of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and later associations with a flaring blazar and the Seyfert galaxy NGC 1068 opened neutrino astronomy. As an astroparticle physicist I find the instrumental audacity of a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice notable.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube; the credit is one name, which understates the contribution of other collaboration leaders and of the DUMAND, AMANDA and Baikal predecessors. A single-laureate prize may be defensible but is vulnerable to dispute.
assessment.maturity: Several source associations are at 3-4 sigma level and the sky map of neutrino emitters is still developing, so the discovery is less mature than the strongest candidates on my ballot.
uncertainties: Source identifications are not yet at overwhelming significance
Whether more than one person deserves credit for experimental realisation
